    Analysis

    Analyse systems, trajectories, and measured data by kind of data.

    The kinds of data are series, paths, fields, agents, and networks.

    AlignmentResult(angles, vectors, positions, order, tensors=None, axes=None, phase=None) dataclass

    A result of alignment, the alignment of the members at every frame.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    angles Array | None

    The angles, frames by members, or None without them.

    		 required
    vectors Array | None

    The vectors or velocities, frames by members by components, or None without them.

    		 required
    positions Array | None

    The positions of agents, frames by agents by dimensions, or None without them.

    		 required
    order Array

    The alignment of every frame, between 0 and 1, or the scalar order of every site of every frame.

    		 required
    tensors Array | None

    The independent components of the tensors, with one frame per row of the first axis, for 'principal-axis'.

    		 None
    axes Array | None

    The principal axis of every site of every frame, with the components on the last axis, for 'principal-axis'.

    		 None
    phase Array | None

    The mean phase of every frame, for 'mean-phase'.

    		 None

    ApplicableAnalysesResult(kinds, readings, analyses) dataclass

    A result of applicable_analyses, the analyses by kind of data.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    kinds list[str]

    The data kinds of the source, in the order agents, field, network, path, series.

    		 required
    readings dict[str, str]

    How the analyses of every data kind read the source, by data kind.

    		 required
    analyses dict[str, list[partial[object]]]

    The analyses that apply to the source by data kind, each bound to its kind for a family, so calling one on the source gives its result.

    		 required

    AutocatalyticSetsResult(snapshots, reactions, products, sizes, fractions, exists) dataclass

    A result of autocatalytic_sets, the largest such set at every frame.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    snapshots list[NetworkSnapshotSpec]

    The network snapshot of every analysed frame.

    		 required
    reactions list[Indices]

    The rows, in the hyperedges of the snapshot, of the reactions of the largest RAF of every frame.

    		 required
    products list[Indices]

    The node rows that the reactions of the largest RAF of every frame produce.

    		 required
    sizes NDArray[int_]

    The number of reactions of the largest RAF of every frame.

    		 required
    fractions Array

    The share of the reactions of every frame that the largest RAF holds, 0 for a frame without reactions.

    		 required
    exists NDArray[bool_]

    Whether every frame holds a RAF.

    		 required

    AutomatonResult(automaton, injective=None, surjective=None, pre_injective=None, pattern=None, inverse=None, composition=None, differences=None, entropy=None, matrix=None, polynomial=None, admissible=None, violations=None, count=None, sample=None) dataclass

    A result of automaton, a decision or a measure of a cellular automaton.

    The cellular automaton is on a finite universe.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    automaton CompositeSystem

    The system.

    		 required
    injective bool | None

    Whether the automaton is injective.

    		 None
    surjective bool | None

    Whether the automaton is surjective.

    		 None
    pre_injective bool | None

    Whether no two configurations that differ only inside the window share their image.

    		 None
    pattern IntArray | None

    A configuration whose values on the window have no preimage, or None when none is found.

    		 None
    inverse CompositeSystem | None

    The system of the inverse automaton with a table rule, or None when the automaton is not injective or no memory up to the radius determines the cells.

    		 None
    composition CompositeSystem | None

    The system of the automaton of the composition, with a function rule.

    		 None
    differences NDArray[bool_] | None

    One row per step, the initial one first, true where the runs differ.

    		 None
    entropy NDArray[float64] | None

    One entropy per window.

    		 None
    matrix Matrix | None

    The Sage matrix of the linear automaton.

    		 None
    polynomial LaurentPolynomial | None

    The Sage Laurent polynomial in the variables x0 to x(d-1).

    		 None
    admissible bool | None

    Whether the configuration belongs to the subshift.

    		 None
    violations NDArray[bool_] | None

    One flag per site, true where a forbidden pattern appears.

    		 None
    count int | None

    The number of configurations without a forbidden pattern.

    		 None
    sample IntArray | None

    The admissible configuration.

    		 None

    CellComplexResult(complex, values, period, betti=None, gradient=None, curl=None, harmonic=None, potential=None, share=None, energy=None) dataclass

    A result of cell_complex, a Hodge decomposition or Betti numbers.

    They are the Hodge decomposition of an edge state, the Betti numbers of a complex, or the curved faces of an angle state.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    complex CellComplexSpace

    The cell complex the analysis reads.

    		 required
    values Array

    The values of the source, with one row per frame.

    		 required
    period float

    The period of the values.

    		 required
    betti tuple[int, ...] | None

    The Betti numbers of every degree, for the kind 'betti'.

    		 None
    gradient Array | None

    The part of every frame that is the exterior derivative of a site potential, for the kind 'hodge'.

    		 None
    curl Array | None

    The part of every frame that the transposed incidence of a face potential gives, for the kind 'hodge'.

    		 None
    harmonic Array | None

    The remainder of every frame, for the kind 'hodge'.

    		 None
    potential Array | None

    The site potential of every frame, of zero mean, for the kind 'hodge'.

    		 None
    share Array | None

    The share of the faces of every frame that are curved, for the kind 'curvature'.

    		 None
    energy Array | None

    The sum over the faces of every frame of one minus the cosine of the oriented sum, for the kind 'curvature'.

    		 None

    ChainShapeResult(positions, values) dataclass

    A result of chain_shape, the geometry of a chain of points per frame.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    positions Array

    The positions, frames by points by dimensions.

    		 required
    values Array

    The value per frame.

    		 required

    ClustersResult(points=None, faces=None, grids=None, graph=None, labels=None, sizes=None, strength=None, mean_size=None, spanning=None, probability=None) dataclass

    A result of clusters, the clusters of a grid, a graph, or points.

    They are the occupied cells of a grid, the components of a graph, or the contacts of points.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    points NDArray[float64] | None

    The arrays of points, one per entry of the first axis, or None for grids and graphs.

    		 None
    faces NDArray[float64] | None

    The sides of the space that holds the points of a trajectory, or None for the bounding box of the points.

    		 None
    grids NDArray[bool_] | None

    The grids, one per entry of the first axis, or None for a graph or points.

    		 None
    graph Graph | None

    The graph, or None for grids and points.

    		 None
    labels IntArray | None

    The label of every cell, 0 for empty cells and 1 onwards for clusters, for 'labels' and for points.

    		 None
    sizes IntArray | None

    The size of every cluster, in label order for 'labels' and largest first otherwise, or None for 'spanning'.

    		 None
    strength float | None

    The share of all sites or nodes in the largest cluster, for 'percolation' and for points.

    		 None
    mean_size float | None

    The mean size of the cluster of an occupied site outside the largest, Σ' s² / Σ' s, for 'percolation' and for points.

    		 None
    spanning bool | None

    Whether a cluster of the grid joins the two opposite edges of axis, always false for graphs, for 'labels', 'percolation', and points.

    		 None
    probability float | None

    The spanning probability of the ensemble, for 'spanning'.

    		 None

    CoarseGrainResult(positions, box, field) dataclass

    A result of coarse_grain, agents as a field or members as a density.

    The field lies on a grid, and the density is over the values of a state.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    positions Array

    The positions, one row per agent, with one leading axis of frames for a trajectory, or the values of the state of every member with over.

    		 required
    box Array | None

    The sides of the box, or None with over.

    		 required
    field Array

    The grid of counts, or of sums with the value components last, with one grid per frame for a trajectory, ready for field analyses, or the fractions of members at every value of over, one row per frame.

    		 required

    ComplexityResult(values, labels, entropy, complexity, minimum, maximum) dataclass

    A result of complexity, places on the complexity and entropy plane.

    It covers every series of a source, or every frame of a field.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    values Array

    The series, one per column, or the frames of the field.

    		 required
    labels list[str]

    The label of every series, or of the field.

    		 required
    entropy Array

    The normalized permutation entropy of every series or frame.

    		 required
    complexity Array

    The statistical complexity of every series or frame.

    		 required
    minimum Array

    The curve of least complexity, one row of entropy and complexity per point.

    		 required
    maximum Array

    The curve of largest complexity, one row of entropy and complexity per point.

    		 required

    CorrelationResult(values, labels, lags=None, correlation=None, time=None, distances=None, length=None, overlap=None) dataclass

    A result of correlation, the correlation of series or of a field.

    It covers every series of a source.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    values Array

    The series, one per column, the ensemble, the field, or the two configurations.

    		 required
    labels list[str]

    The label of every series, of the ensemble or field, or of the two configurations.

    		 required
    lags Array | None

    The lags in time, for 'auto'.

    		 None
    correlation Array | None

    One autocorrelation per series for 'auto', one row per waiting time and one column per lag for 'two-time', and the correlation at every distance for 'function'.

    		 None
    time Array | None

    The integrated autocorrelation time of every series, for 'auto'.

    		 None
    distances Array | None

    The distances, for 'function'.

    		 None
    length float | Array | None

    The correlation length, for 'length'.

    		 None
    overlap float | Array | None

    The overlap of the two configurations, one per frame for frames, for 'overlap'.

    		 None

    DataCollapseResult(values, labels, critical=None, nu=None, exponent=None, quality=None, time_spread=None, ratio_spread=None, ratios=None, densities=None, spread=None, crossings=None) dataclass

    A result of data_collapse, curves of several sizes collapsed onto one.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    values dict[float, Array] | Array

    The curve of every size, the curves of every waiting time, or the samples of every age.

    		 required
    labels list[float]

    The size, waiting time, or age of every curve.

    		 required
    critical float | None

    The critical value used or fitted, for 'scaling'.

    		 None
    nu float | None

    The correlation length exponent used or fitted, for 'scaling'.

    		 None
    exponent float | None

    The exponent a used or fitted, for 'scaling'.

    		 None
    quality float | None

    The mean squared relative distance between the scaled curves, 0 for a perfect collapse, for 'scaling'.

    		 None
    time_spread float | None

    The largest difference between the curves against the lag, 0 without aging, for 'aging'.

    		 None
    ratio_spread float | None

    The largest difference between the curves against tau / t_w, 0 under simple aging, for 'aging'.

    		 None
    ratios Array | None

    The centres of the bins of tau / t, for 'distribution'.

    		 None
    densities Array | None

    One row per age of t P(tau, t) on the bins, for 'distribution'.

    		 None
    spread float | None

    The largest relative difference between the rows where every row is positive, for 'distribution'.

    		 None
    crossings Array | None

    The first crossing of the curves of every pair of consecutive sizes, nan where they do not cross, for 'crossings'.

    		 None

    DefectsResult(angles, positions, charges) dataclass

    A result of defects, the point defects of a field of angles.

    They come with their topological charges.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    angles Array

    The angles, with one frame per row of the first axis.

    		 required
    positions list[Array]

    The centres of the plaquettes with a defect at every frame, each an array of defects by dimensions.

    		 required
    charges list[Array]

    The charges of the defects at every frame, each an array in the order of positions.

    		 required

    DisplacementResult(positions, lags, msd, exponent, diffusion) dataclass

    A result of displacement, the mean squared displacement over lags.

    It comes with its scaling exponent and the diffusion coefficient.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    positions Array

    The unwrapped positions, frames by particles by dimensions.

    		 required
    lags Array

    The lags in time.

    		 required
    msd Array

    The mean squared displacement at every lag.

    		 required
    exponent float

    The slope of log msd against log lag over the fit range, 1 for normal diffusion, below 1 for subdiffusion, and above 1 for superdiffusion.

    		 required
    diffusion float

    The coefficient D of msd = 2 d D lag fitted over the fit range in d dimensions.

    		 required

    DistributionResult(values, labels, edges=None, density=None, support=None, survival=None, mean=None, variance=None, skewness=None, kurtosis=None, ratio=None, cumulant=None, index=None, gini=None, tail_index=None, records=None, distance=None) dataclass

    		 None

    		 None
    survival Array | None

    The share of samples at or above every distinct value, P(X >= x), for 'ccdf'.

    		 None
    mean Array | None

    The mean of every sample, for 'moments'.

    		 None
    variance Array | None

    The variance of every sample, for 'moments'.

    		 None
    skewness Array | None

    The skewness of every sample, for 'moments'.

    		 None
    kurtosis Array | None

    The excess kurtosis of every sample, 0 for Gaussian samples, for 'moments'.

    		 None
    ratio Array | None

    The moment ratio of every sample, for 'moment-ratio'.

    		 None
    cumulant Array | None

    The normalized cumulant of every sample, for 'moment-ratio'.

    		 None
    index Array | None

    The dispersion index of every sample, for 'dispersion-index'.

    		 None
    gini float | None

    The Gini coefficient, for 'gini'.

    		 None
    tail_index float | None

    The Hill estimate of the tail index, for 'tail-index'.

    		 None
    records NDArray[int64] | None

    The number of records of every series, the first value included, for 'records'.

    		 None
    distance float | None

    The total variation distance between the two groups, for 'total-variation'.

    		 None

    DomainsResult(frames, times, size=None, exponent=None, wavelength=None, wavenumber=None, orientation=None, density=None) dataclass

    The delay in steps.

    dimension int | None

    points Array | None

    EmergenceResult(matrix=None, values=None, labels=None, information=None, determinism=None, degeneracy=None, states=None, partition=None, macro_matrix=None, micro_information=None, macro_information=None, gain=None, psi=None, delta=None, gamma=None, macro_uncertainty=None, micro_uncertainty=None, gap=None) dataclass

    A result of emergence, the emergence of a macro scale over a micro scale.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    matrix Array | None

    The micro transition matrix, for 'effective-information' and 'causal'.

    		 None
    values AnyArray | None

    The micro series, one column per micro variable, for 'criteria' and 'closure'.

    		 None
    labels list[str] | None

    The label of every micro series.

    		 None
    information float | None

    The effective information in bits, for 'effective-information'.

    		 None
    determinism float | None

    log2 n minus the mean entropy of the rows, high when every state has one successor.

    		 None
    degeneracy float | None

    log2 n minus the entropy of the mean row, high when many states share a successor.

    		 None
    states NDArray[int64] | None

    The states with observed transitions, the rows the effective information uses.

    		 None
    partition IntArray | None

    The macro label of every micro state, for 'causal'.

    		 None
    macro_matrix Array | None

    The macro transition matrix of the partition, every row summing to one.

    		 None
    micro_information float | None

    The effective information of the micro matrix.

    		 None
    macro_information float | None

    The effective information of the macro matrix.

    		 None
    gain float | None

    The macro minus the micro effective information in bits.

    		 None
    psi float | None

    I(V_t ; V_t') - Σ_j I(X_t^j ; V_t'), positive when the macro feature predicts its own future beyond what every micro variable does, a sufficient condition for causal emergence.

    		 None
    delta float | None

    max_j [I(V_t ; X_t'^j) - Σ_i I(X_t^i ; X_t'^j)], positive when the macro feature predicts a micro variable beyond the micro variables, a sufficient condition for downward causation.

    alignment(source, *, kind='mean-vector', variables=None, group=None, vectors=False)

    Return the alignment of the members of a source at every frame, of one kind.

    The members are the agents of a group, the sites of a field, or the columns of a set of series, and each holds an angle or a vector. A trajectory gives the agents of a group with their directions or phases, velocities, and positions, else every frame of a field of angles, or of vectors with vectors=True, else the series of variables or the states with the role 'phase', one column per member and one row per sample.

    • 'mean-vector': the length of the mean unit vector, 1 when every member points the same way and about 1 / sqrt(n) for random directions. It reads vectors when the source has them, and angles otherwise.
    • 'mean-rotation': the mean normalized angular momentum of agents about their centre in a plane, 1 when every agent turns the same way and near 0 for a polarized or disordered group. It reads positions and velocities.
    • 'axial': |<exp(2 i theta)>| of the angles, which ignores the sign of a direction.
    • 'mean-phase': the modulus r and the argument psi of the mean r exp(i psi) = <exp(i theta)> of the angles, the synchrony and the mean phase.
    • 'principal-axis': the eigenvector of the largest eigenvalue of a symmetric tensor at every site, axes, and the scalar order of the tensor at every site, order. It reads a field of a symmetric tensor state, or an array of its independent components on the last axis, whose number gives the symmetry and the dimension: 2 and 5 for a symmetric traceless tensor in 2 and 3 dimensions, and 3 and 6 for a symmetric tensor.

    Angles are derived from the first two components of vectors when a source has no angles, and a vector of one component points at the angle 0 or pi by its sign. An array of angles holds one snapshot when it has one dimension, and one frame per row of its first axis otherwise, every other axis indexing members. An array of vectors, with vectors=True, holds the components along its last axis, and one snapshot when it has two dimensions. An array for 'mean-rotation' holds the positions followed by the velocities of every agent along its last axis.

    It appears in many fields. It measures how well birds of a flock fly together, how spins of a magnet line up, and how cells of a tissue orient.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    source Source

    The trajectory, or an array of angles, vectors, positions and velocities, or tensor components.

    		 required
    kind str

    The alignment to compute, one of the kinds above.

    		 'mean-vector'
    variables Sequence[str] | None

    The field or the series of a trajectory to read, or None for its agents, or else its first field, its states with the role 'phase', or its scalar series.

    		 None
    group str | None

    The path of the agent group of a trajectory, or None for the first one.

    		 None
    vectors bool

    Whether the members hold vectors rather than angles.

    		 False

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    result AlignmentResult

    The members read and their alignment at every frame.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    AnalysisError

    The kind is unknown, a setting the kind does not read is changed, the trajectory holds no kind of data the function reads, or the source lacks what the kind needs.

    Examples:

    >>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import alignment
>>> alignment([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]).order.tolist()
[1.0]
>>> alignment([0.0, np.pi], kind='axial').order.round(6).tolist()
[1.0]
>>> angles = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 8, endpoint=False)
>>> ring = np.column_stack([np.cos(angles), np.sin(angles)])
>>> mill = np.hstack([ring, np.column_stack([-ring[:, 1], ring[:, 0]])])
>>> alignment(mill, kind='mean-rotation').order.round(6).tolist()
[1.0]
>>> phases = alignment([[0.5, 0.5], [0.0, np.pi]], kind='mean-phase')
>>> phases.order.round(6).tolist(), phases.phase.round(6)[:1].tolist()
([1.0, 0.0], [0.5])
>>> alignment([[0.5, 0.0], [0.0, 0.5]], kind='principal-axis').order.tolist()
[[1.0, 1.0]]

    def alignment(
    source: Source,
    *,
    kind: str = 'mean-vector',
    variables: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    group: str | None = None,
    vectors: bool = False,
) -> AlignmentResult:
    """Return the alignment of the members of a source at every frame, of one kind.

    The members are the agents of a group, the sites of a field, or the columns of a set of series, and each holds an
    angle or a vector. A trajectory gives the agents of a group with their directions or phases, velocities, and
    positions, else every frame of a field of angles, or of vectors with `vectors=True`, else the series of `variables`
    or the states with the role `'phase'`, one column per member and one row per sample.

    - `'mean-vector'`: the length of the mean unit vector, 1 when every member points the same way and about
      `1 / sqrt(n)` for random directions. It reads vectors when the source has them, and angles otherwise.
    - `'mean-rotation'`: the mean normalized angular momentum of agents about their centre in a plane, 1 when every
      agent turns the same way and near 0 for a polarized or disordered group. It reads positions and velocities.
    - `'axial'`: `|<exp(2 i theta)>|` of the angles, which ignores the sign of a direction.
    - `'mean-phase'`: the modulus `r` and the argument `psi` of the mean `r exp(i psi) = <exp(i theta)>` of the
      angles, the synchrony and the mean phase.
    - `'principal-axis'`: the eigenvector of the largest eigenvalue of a symmetric tensor at every site, `axes`, and
      the scalar order of the tensor at every site, `order`. It reads a field of a symmetric tensor state, or an array
      of its independent components on the last axis, whose number gives the symmetry and the dimension: 2 and 5 for a
      symmetric traceless tensor in 2 and 3 dimensions, and 3 and 6 for a symmetric tensor.

    Angles are derived from the first two components of vectors when a source has no angles, and a vector of one
    component points at the angle 0 or `pi` by its sign. An array of angles holds
    one snapshot when it has one dimension, and one frame per row of its first axis otherwise, every other axis
    indexing members. An array of vectors, with `vectors=True`, holds the components along its last axis, and one
    snapshot when it has two dimensions. An array for `'mean-rotation'` holds the positions followed by the
    velocities of every agent along its last axis.

    It appears in many fields. It measures how well birds of a flock fly together, how spins of a magnet line up, and
    how cells of a tissue orient.

    Args:
        source:
            The trajectory, or an array of angles, vectors, positions and velocities, or tensor components.

        kind:
            The alignment to compute, one of the kinds above.

        variables:
            The field or the series of a trajectory to read, or `None` for its agents, or else its first field, its
            states with the role `'phase'`, or its scalar series.

        group:
            The path of the agent group of a trajectory, or `None` for the first one.

        vectors:
            Whether the members hold vectors rather than angles.

    Returns:
        result:
            The members read and their alignment at every frame.

    Raises:
        AnalysisError:
            The kind is unknown, a setting the kind does not read is changed, the trajectory holds no kind of data the
            function reads, or the source lacks what the kind needs.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import alignment
        >>> alignment([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]).order.tolist()
        [1.0]
        >>> alignment([0.0, np.pi], kind='axial').order.round(6).tolist()
        [1.0]
        >>> angles = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 8, endpoint=False)
        >>> ring = np.column_stack([np.cos(angles), np.sin(angles)])
        >>> mill = np.hstack([ring, np.column_stack([-ring[:, 1], ring[:, 0]])])
        >>> alignment(mill, kind='mean-rotation').order.round(6).tolist()
        [1.0]
        >>> phases = alignment([[0.5, 0.5], [0.0, np.pi]], kind='mean-phase')
        >>> phases.order.round(6).tolist(), phases.phase.round(6)[:1].tolist()
        ([1.0, 0.0], [0.5])
        >>> alignment([[0.5, 0.0], [0.0, 0.5]], kind='principal-axis').order.tolist()
        [[1.0, 1.0]]
    """
    _check_choice('alignment', 'kind', kind, KINDS)
    _check_settings(alignment, 'kind', SETTINGS[kind], kind=kind, variables=variables, group=group, vectors=vectors)
    if isinstance(source, Trajectory):
        angles, velocities, positions, tensors = _read_trajectory(source, kind, variables, group, vectors=vectors)
    else:
        angles, velocities, positions, tensors = _read_array(source, kind, vectors=vectors)
    if kind == 'principal-axis':
        axes, order = _principal_axis(tensors)
        return AlignmentResult(angles, velocities, positions, order, tensors=tensors, axes=axes)
    derived = angles
    if derived is None and velocities is not None:
        across = velocities[..., 1] if velocities.shape[-1] > 1 else np.zeros_like(velocities[..., 0])
        derived = np.arctan2(across, velocities[..., 0])
    error_msg = (
        f'alignment of kind {kind!r} needs the angles, vectors, or positions that the source lacks. Use a source with '
        'them.'
    )
    if kind == 'mean-rotation':
        if positions is None or velocities is None:
            raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
        return AlignmentResult(angles, velocities, positions, _mean_rotation(positions, velocities))
    if derived is None:
        raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
    if kind == 'mean-vector':
        order = (
            _mean_vector_length(velocities, vectors=True) if velocities is not None else _mean_vector_length(derived)
        )
        return AlignmentResult(angles, velocities, positions, order)
    if kind == 'axial':
        return AlignmentResult(angles, velocities, positions, _axial_order(derived))
    mean = _mean_phase(derived)
    return AlignmentResult(angles, velocities, positions, np.abs(mean), phase=np.angle(mean))

    Return the analyses that apply to a trajectory, a system, or an array.

When the source is a system, or a trajectory of one, an analysis whose capability tags the system lacks, such as lyapunov of a stochastic system, is left out. A one-dimensional array is one series, and an array of more dimensions is one field and a set of series, one per column.

    It appears in every study that starts from a run or a data set and asks which measures fit it.

>>> found.readings['series']
'every column of the array as a series'

    def applicable_analyses(source: Source) -> ApplicableAnalysesResult:
    """Return the analyses that apply to a trajectory, a system, or an array.

    They are listed under the kind of data they read. The kinds of data the source holds are read first. Every analysis
    of the library that takes no required setting is bound once per kind of a family, and those whose data kind the
    source holds are kept, as the tags the module of every analysis declares give it. When the source is a system, or a
    trajectory of one, an analysis whose capability tags the system lacks, such as `lyapunov` of a stochastic system, is
    left out. A one-dimensional array is one series, and an array of more dimensions is one field and a set of series,
    one per column.

    It appears in every study that starts from a run or a data set and asks which measures fit it.

    Args:
        source:
            The trajectory, the system, the graph, or the array.

    Returns:
        result:
            The data kinds of the source, how they are read, and the analyses of every kind.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import applicable_analyses
        >>> found = applicable_analyses(np.zeros((16, 16)))
        >>> found.kinds
        ['field', 'series']
        >>> found.readings['series']
        'every column of the array as a series'
        >>> any(item.func.__name__ == 'entropy' for item in found.analyses['series'])
        True
    """
    source = _composite(source)
    kinds = [str(kind) for kind in _get_data_kinds(source)]
    if isinstance(source, Trajectory | CompositeSystem | nx.Graph | NetworkSnapshotSpec):
        readings = {kind: DataKind(kind).reading for kind in kinds}
    else:
        readings = {kind: _get_array_reading(DataKind(kind), np.ndim(source)) for kind in kinds}
    tags = _get_source_tags(source)
    analyses: dict[str, list[partial[object]]] = {kind: [] for kind in kinds}
    for function in ANALYSES:
        parameters = list(inspect.signature(function).parameters.values())[1:]
        if any(parameter.default is inspect.Parameter.empty for parameter in parameters):
            continue
        family = getattr(sys.modules[function.__module__], 'KINDS', None)
        if family is not None and any(parameter.name == 'kind' for parameter in parameters):
            bound = [(bind_analysis(function, kind=kind), _get_analysis_tags(function, kind)) for kind in family]
        else:
            bound = [(bind_analysis(function), _get_analysis_tags(function))]
        for analysis, needed in bound:
            if needed.data in analyses and (tags is None or not needed.get_missing(tags)):
                analyses[needed.data].append(analysis)
    return ApplicableAnalysesResult(kinds, readings, analyses)

    autocatalytic_sets(source, *, food=None, frames=None)

    Return the maximal autocatalytic set of a catalytic reaction network.

    The set is found at every frame. The method is that of Hordijk and Steel. The network is a network snapshot whose hyperedges are the reactions and whose directed edges are the catalysis. Every hyperedge produces its last member from its other members, the reactants, and an edge from a node c to a node p makes c a catalyst of every reaction that produces p, as goods catalyse the production of other goods in the TAP model of Hordijk and Kauffman (2022). A set of reactions is reflexively autocatalytic and food-generated, a RAF, when every reaction has a catalyst produced by the set or in the food set, and every reactant is reachable from the food set by reactions of the set. The algorithm of Hordijk and Steel (2004) finds the largest RAF, the union of every RAF: it removes the reactions with a reactant outside the closure of the food set, or without a catalyst in it, until no reaction is removed, and returns the reactions left, an empty set when there is no RAF.

    It appears in studies of the origin of life, where sets of molecules catalyse their own production, and in models of economies whose goods are made from each other.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    source Source

    The network snapshot, or the trajectory of a network whose hyperedges change.

    		 required
    food Sequence[int] | None

    The node rows of the food set, or None for the nodes present that no reaction produces.

    		 None
    frames Sequence[int] | None

    The frames of a trajectory to analyse, or None for every frame.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    result AutocatalyticSetsResult

    The snapshots, and the reactions, products, size, and share of the largest RAF of every frame.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    AnalysisError

    The source is neither a network snapshot nor a trajectory of a network whose hyperedges change.

    Examples:

    >>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import autocatalytic_sets
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import NetworkSnapshotSpec
>>> nodes = np.arange(5)
>>> reactions = np.array([[0, 1, 2], [2, 0, 3], [3, 1, 4]])
>>> sources, targets = np.array([3, 4, 0]), np.array([2, 3, 4])
>>> snapshot = NetworkSnapshotSpec(nodes, sources, targets, np.arange(3), reactions)
>>> result = autocatalytic_sets(snapshot)
>>> result.reactions[0].tolist(), result.products[0].tolist()
([0, 1, 2], [2, 3, 4])
>>> uncatalysed = NetworkSnapshotSpec(nodes, sources[:2], targets[:2], np.arange(2), reactions)
>>> autocatalytic_sets(uncatalysed).exists.tolist()
[False]

    def autocatalytic_sets(
    source: Source,
    *,
    food: Sequence[int] | None = None,
    frames: Sequence[int] | None = None,
) -> AutocatalyticSetsResult:
    """Return the maximal autocatalytic set of a catalytic reaction network.

    The set is found at every frame. The method is that of Hordijk and Steel. The network is a network snapshot whose
    hyperedges are the reactions and whose directed edges are the catalysis. Every hyperedge produces its last member
    from its other members, the reactants, and an edge from a node `c` to a node `p` makes `c` a catalyst of every
    reaction that produces `p`, as goods catalyse the production of other goods in the TAP model of Hordijk and Kauffman
    (2022). A set of reactions is reflexively autocatalytic and food-generated, a RAF, when every reaction has a
    catalyst produced by the set or in the food set, and every reactant is reachable from the food set by reactions of
    the set. The algorithm of Hordijk and Steel (2004) finds the largest RAF, the union of every RAF: it removes the
    reactions with a reactant outside the closure of the food set, or without a catalyst in it, until no reaction is
    removed, and returns the reactions left, an empty set when there is no RAF.

    It appears in studies of the origin of life, where sets of molecules catalyse their own production, and in models of
    economies whose goods are made from each other.

    Args:
        source:
            The network snapshot, or the trajectory of a network whose hyperedges change.

        food:
            The node rows of the food set, or `None` for the nodes present that no reaction produces.

        frames:
            The frames of a trajectory to analyse, or `None` for every frame.

    Returns:
        result:
            The snapshots, and the reactions, products, size, and share of the largest RAF of every frame.

    Raises:
        AnalysisError:
            The source is neither a network snapshot nor a trajectory of a network whose hyperedges change.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import autocatalytic_sets
        >>> from skcomplex.core.specs import NetworkSnapshotSpec
        >>> nodes = np.arange(5)
        >>> reactions = np.array([[0, 1, 2], [2, 0, 3], [3, 1, 4]])
        >>> sources, targets = np.array([3, 4, 0]), np.array([2, 3, 4])
        >>> snapshot = NetworkSnapshotSpec(nodes, sources, targets, np.arange(3), reactions)
        >>> result = autocatalytic_sets(snapshot)
        >>> result.reactions[0].tolist(), result.products[0].tolist()
        ([0, 1, 2], [2, 3, 4])
        >>> uncatalysed = NetworkSnapshotSpec(nodes, sources[:2], targets[:2], np.arange(2), reactions)
        >>> autocatalytic_sets(uncatalysed).exists.tolist()
        [False]
    """
    if isinstance(source, NetworkSnapshotSpec):
        snapshots = [source]
    elif isinstance(source, Trajectory):
        chosen = range(len(source.times)) if frames is None else frames
        snapshots = [source.get_network(int(frame)) for frame in chosen]
    else:
        error_msg = f'Autocatalytic sets are read from a network snapshot or a trajectory, not {type(source).__name__}.'
        raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
    if any(snapshot.hyperedges is None for snapshot in snapshots):
        error_msg = (
            'Autocatalytic sets read the reactions as hyperedges that change. Give the network a variable group on '
            'its hyperedges.'
        )
        raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
    found = [_largest_raf(snapshot, food) for snapshot in snapshots]
    reactions = [rows for rows, _ in found]
    sizes = np.asarray([rows.size for rows in reactions], dtype=int)
    totals = np.asarray([len(_reactions_of(snapshot)) for snapshot in snapshots])
    fractions = np.divide(sizes, totals, out=np.zeros(len(totals)), where=totals > 0)
    return AutocatalyticSetsResult(
        snapshots,
        reactions,
        [products for _, products in found],
        sizes,
        fractions,
        sizes > 0,
    )

    automaton(source, *, kind='injective', method='auto', window=None, infinite=False, tries=200, random_state=None, max_radius=2, second=None, configuration=None, site=0, steps=1, windows=None, base=2.0, sweeps=100)

    Return a decision or a measure of a cellular automaton or subshift of a system.

    The function reads a CompositeSystem. An automaton is a group of cells with one synchronous and deterministic LocalRuleInteraction, and it is linear when the rule is a LinearRuleSpec. The number of values of a cell comes from the finite domain of the state, or else from the rule. A subshift is a group with a state whose domain is a SubshiftSpec.

    • 'injective', 'surjective', and 'pre-injective': whether two different configurations never share their image, whether every configuration has a preimage, which on a finite universe holds exactly when it is injective, and whether two configurations that differ only inside a window never share their image. Small universes are decided by enumerating every configuration, and larger ones by a SAT encoding solved by PySAT. A linear automaton is decided from its matrix, all three holding exactly when the matrix is invertible, or on Z^d from its Laurent polynomial, injective when it is a monomial and surjective and pre-injective when it is not zero.
    • 'garden-of-eden': a pattern on a window that no configuration maps to. Small universes enumerate the images of every configuration, and larger ones draw random patterns and keep the first one whose preimage constraints a SAT solver finds unsatisfiable.
    • 'inverse': an automaton whose composition with a reversible automaton is the identity, with the smallest memory. The search tries the neighbourhoods of every radius up to max_radius, a box of offsets on a lattice or the ball of group elements on a group space, and keeps the first on which the image determines every cell.
    • 'compose': the automaton that applies the automaton and then second on the same space, whose neighbourhood holds the composite t s of every element t read by the second and s read by the first.
    • 'difference': where two runs differ when one starts from configuration and the other from it with the cell at site changed to its next value modulo the number of states.
    • 'entropy': the entropy log |X_F| / |F| of the configurations of a subshift, or of the image of an automaton whose rule and neighbourhood are applied on every window. X_F is the set of admissible configurations of a window F, or the set of images on the sites of F whose cells lie inside it. Along a Følner sequence of windows the values approach the topological entropy.
    • 'matrix': the square matrix of a linear automaton over its field, whose row g gives the image at g.
    • 'polynomial': the Laurent polynomial sum a_s x^s of a linear automaton on a lattice, its symbol on Z^d.
    • 'admissible' and 'violations': whether no forbidden pattern appears in configuration, and the sites at which one appears.
    • 'count': the number of admissible configurations of the space of a subshift, by dynamic programming over its sites. The counts of completions are shared between assignments that agree on the earlier sites that later patterns read, so a window of a one-dimensional subshift costs linear time.
    • 'sample': an admissible configuration drawn by a Markov chain of single-cell moves that keep it admissible, from configuration, or from every cell at 0.

    It appears in mathematics and computer science, where it decides whether a cellular automaton loses information, and in physics, where reversible automata model conservative dynamics.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    source Source

    The system of the automaton or of the subshift.

    		 required
    kind str

    The decision or measure, one of the kinds above.

    		 'injective'
    method str

    'enumeration', 'sat', or 'auto' to enumerate up to MAX_CONFIGURATIONS configurations.

    		 'auto'
    window Sequence[int] | None

    The sites where configurations may differ, or of the Garden of Eden pattern, or None for every site.

    		 None
    infinite bool

    Whether to decide a linear automaton on Z^d from its Laurent polynomial instead of on its space.

    		 False
    tries int

    The number of random patterns tried by SAT.

    		 200
    random_state int | Generator | None

    The seed or generator of the random patterns or of the moves of a sample.

    		 None
    max_radius int

    The largest radius of the memory of the inverse.

    		 2
    second CompositeSystem | None

    The system of the automaton applied after the analysed one.

    		 None
    configuration ArrayLike | None

    The values of the sites: the initial ones of the difference pattern or of a sample, or the ones checked.

    		 None
    site int

    The site of the changed cell.

    		 0
    steps int

    The number of steps of the difference pattern.

    		 1
    windows Sequence[BaseSpace] | None

    The windows of the entropy, such as lattices with fixed edges of growing size.

    		 None
    base float

    The base of the logarithm.

    		 2.0
    sweeps int

    The number of sweeps of a sample, each proposing a random value at every site in a random order.

    		 100

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    result AutomatonResult

    The system and the decision or measure of the kind.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    AnalysisError

    The system holds nothing the kind reads, the method is unknown, enumeration is asked for too many configurations, composed automata differ in space or number of states, the rule returns a value outside the states, a linear automaton has a matrix on a ball or a polynomial without offsets, or the initial configuration of a sample is not admissible.

    Examples:

    >>> from typing import Annotated
>>> from sage.sets.finite_enumerated_set import FiniteEnumeratedSet
>>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import automaton
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, GroupElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import LocalRuleInteraction
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import BallNeighborhood, LatticeNeighborhood, LatticeSpace
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec, SubshiftSpec, TableSpec, TotalisticSpec
>>> class CellElement(Element):
...     def __init__(self, label, alive: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=FiniteEnumeratedSet([0, 1]))] = 0):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.alive = alive
>>> def build(size, rule, neighborhood):
...     cells = GroupElement('cells', element=CellElement, space=LatticeSpace(size), on='sites')
...     interaction = LocalRuleInteraction(
...         'rule', target='cells', state='alive', rule=rule, neighborhood=neighborhood
...     )
...     return CompositeSystem(elements=[cells], interactions=[interaction])
>>> shift = build(8, TableSpec({(1,): 1}), LatticeNeighborhood(((1,),)))
>>> automaton(shift).injective
True
>>> majority = build(5, TotalisticSpec(lambda total: total >= 2), BallNeighborhood(n_dim=1, center='inline'))
>>> automaton(majority, kind='garden-of-eden').pattern.tolist()
[0, 0, 1, 0, 1]
>>> class GoldenCellElement(Element):
...     def __init__(
...         self,
...         label,
...         alive: Annotated[
...             float, StateSpec(domain=SubshiftSpec(LatticeNeighborhood(((0,), (1,))), ((1, 1),)))
...         ] = 0,
...     ):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.alive = alive
>>> window = LatticeSpace(6, boundary='fixed')
>>> cells = GroupElement('cells', element=GoldenCellElement, space=window, on='sites')
>>> golden = CompositeSystem(elements=[cells])
>>> automaton(golden, kind='count').count
21
>>> windows = [LatticeSpace(20, boundary='fixed')]
>>> automaton(golden, kind='entropy', windows=windows).entropy.round(3).tolist()
[0.706]

    def automaton(
    source: Source,
    *,
    kind: str = 'injective',
    method: str = 'auto',
    window: Sequence[int] | None = None,
    infinite: bool = False,
    tries: int = 200,
    random_state: int | np.random.Generator | None = None,
    max_radius: int = 2,
    second: CompositeSystem | None = None,
    configuration: npt.ArrayLike | None = None,
    site: int = 0,
    steps: int = 1,
    windows: Sequence[BaseSpace] | None = None,
    base: float = 2.0,
    sweeps: int = 100,
) -> AutomatonResult:
    """Return a decision or a measure of a cellular automaton or subshift of a system.

    The function reads a `CompositeSystem`. An automaton is a group of cells with one synchronous and deterministic
    `LocalRuleInteraction`, and it is linear when the rule is a `LinearRuleSpec`. The number of values of a cell comes
    from the finite domain of the state, or else from the rule. A subshift is a group with a state whose domain is a
    `SubshiftSpec`.

    - `'injective'`, `'surjective'`, and `'pre-injective'`: whether two different configurations never share their
      image, whether every configuration has a preimage, which on a finite universe holds exactly when it is
      injective, and whether two configurations that differ only inside a window never share their image. Small
      universes are decided by enumerating every configuration, and larger ones by a SAT encoding solved by PySAT. A
      linear automaton is decided from its matrix, all three holding exactly when the matrix is invertible, or on
      `Z^d` from its Laurent polynomial, injective when it is a monomial and surjective and pre-injective when it is
      not zero.
    - `'garden-of-eden'`: a pattern on a window that no configuration maps to. Small universes enumerate the images of
      every configuration, and larger ones draw random patterns and keep the first one whose preimage constraints a
      SAT solver finds unsatisfiable.
    - `'inverse'`: an automaton whose composition with a reversible automaton is the identity, with the smallest
      memory. The search tries the neighbourhoods of every radius up to `max_radius`, a box of offsets on a lattice or
      the ball of group elements on a group space, and keeps the first on which the image determines every cell.
    - `'compose'`: the automaton that applies the automaton and then `second` on the same space, whose neighbourhood
      holds the composite `t s` of every element `t` read by the second and `s` read by the first.
    - `'difference'`: where two runs differ when one starts from `configuration` and the other from it with the cell
      at `site` changed to its next value modulo the number of states.
    - `'entropy'`: the entropy `log |X_F| / |F|` of the configurations of a subshift, or of the image of an automaton
      whose rule and neighbourhood are applied on every window. `X_F` is the set of admissible configurations of a
      window `F`, or the set of images on the sites of `F` whose cells lie inside it. Along a Følner sequence of
      windows the values approach the topological entropy.
    - `'matrix'`: the square matrix of a linear automaton over its field, whose row `g` gives the image at `g`.
    - `'polynomial'`: the Laurent polynomial `sum a_s x^s` of a linear automaton on a lattice, its symbol on `Z^d`.
    - `'admissible'` and `'violations'`: whether no forbidden pattern appears in `configuration`, and the sites at
      which one appears.
    - `'count'`: the number of admissible configurations of the space of a subshift, by dynamic programming over its
      sites. The counts of completions are shared between assignments that agree on the earlier sites that later
      patterns read, so a window of a one-dimensional subshift costs linear time.
    - `'sample'`: an admissible configuration drawn by a Markov chain of single-cell moves that keep it admissible,
      from `configuration`, or from every cell at 0.

    It appears in mathematics and computer science, where it decides whether a cellular automaton loses information, and
    in physics, where reversible automata model conservative dynamics.

    Args:
        source:
            The system of the automaton or of the subshift.

        kind:
            The decision or measure, one of the kinds above.

        method:
            `'enumeration'`, `'sat'`, or `'auto'` to enumerate up to `MAX_CONFIGURATIONS` configurations.

        window:
            The sites where configurations may differ, or of the Garden of Eden pattern, or `None` for every site.

            The seed or generator of the random patterns or of the moves of a sample.

            The largest radius of the memory of the inverse.

            The system of the automaton applied after the analysed one.

            The site of the changed cell.

            The windows of the entropy, such as lattices with fixed edges of growing size.

            The base of the logarithm.

            The system and the decision or measure of the kind.

    Raises:
        AnalysisError:
            The system holds nothing the kind reads, the method is unknown, enumeration is asked for too many
            configurations, composed automata differ in space or number of states, the rule returns a value outside the
            states, a linear automaton has a matrix on a ball or a polynomial without offsets, or the initial
            configuration of a sample is not admissible.

    Examples:
        >>> from typing import Annotated
        >>> from sage.sets.finite_enumerated_set import FiniteEnumeratedSet
        >>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import automaton
        >>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, GroupElement
        >>> from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import LocalRuleInteraction
        >>> from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import BallNeighborhood, LatticeNeighborhood, LatticeSpace
        >>> from skcomplex.core.components.systems import CompositeSystem
        >>> from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec, SubshiftSpec, TableSpec, TotalisticSpec
        >>> class CellElement(Element):
        ...     def __init__(self, label, alive: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=FiniteEnumeratedSet([0, 1]))] = 0):
        ...         super().__init__(label)
        ...         self.alive = alive
        >>> def build(size, rule, neighborhood):
        ...     cells = GroupElement('cells', element=CellElement, space=LatticeSpace(size), on='sites')
        ...     interaction = LocalRuleInteraction(
        ...         'rule', target='cells', state='alive', rule=rule, neighborhood=neighborhood
        ...     )
        ...     return CompositeSystem(elements=[cells], interactions=[interaction])
        >>> shift = build(8, TableSpec({(1,): 1}), LatticeNeighborhood(((1,),)))
        >>> automaton(shift).injective
        True
        >>> majority = build(5, TotalisticSpec(lambda total: total >= 2), BallNeighborhood(n_dim=1, center='inline'))
        >>> automaton(majority, kind='garden-of-eden').pattern.tolist()
        [0, 0, 1, 0, 1]
        >>> class GoldenCellElement(Element):
        ...     def __init__(
        ...         self,
        ...         label,
        ...         alive: Annotated[
        ...             float, StateSpec(domain=SubshiftSpec(LatticeNeighborhood(((0,), (1,))), ((1, 1),)))
        ...         ] = 0,
        ...     ):
        ...         super().__init__(label)
        ...         self.alive = alive
        >>> window = LatticeSpace(6, boundary='fixed')
        >>> cells = GroupElement('cells', element=GoldenCellElement, space=window, on='sites')
        >>> golden = CompositeSystem(elements=[cells])
        >>> automaton(golden, kind='count').count
        21
        >>> windows = [LatticeSpace(20, boundary='fixed')]
        >>> automaton(golden, kind='entropy', windows=windows).entropy.round(3).tolist()
        [0.706]
    """
    source = _composite(source)
    _check_choice('automaton', 'kind', kind, KINDS)
    _check_settings(
        automaton,
        'kind',
        SETTINGS[kind],
        kind=kind,
        method=method,
        window=window,
        infinite=infinite,
        tries=tries,
        random_state=random_state,
        max_radius=max_radius,
        second=second,
        configuration=configuration,
        site=site,
        steps=steps,
        windows=windows,
        base=base,
        sweeps=sweeps,
    )
    if method not in METHODS:
        error_msg = f'automaton has method={method!r}. Use one of {", ".join(METHODS)}.'
        raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
    needed = {
        'compose': ('second', second),
        'difference': ('configuration', configuration),
        'entropy': ('windows', windows),
        'admissible': ('configuration', configuration),
        'violations': ('configuration', configuration),
    }.get(kind)
    if needed is not None and needed[1] is None:
        error_msg = f'automaton of kind {kind!r} needs {needed[0]}. Give it.'
        raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
    sources = SOURCES[kind]
    error_msg = (
        f'automaton of kind {kind!r} reads a system with {" or ".join(sources)}, not {type(source).__name__}. Build '
        'one of them.'
    )
    if not isinstance(source, CompositeSystem):
        raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
    found = _find_subshift(source)
    rule = _find_rule(source)
    if found is not None and SUBSHIFT in sources:
        return _run_subshift(
            source,
            kind,
            found[1],
            _get_space(source, found[0]),
            configuration=configuration,
            windows=windows,
            base=base,
            sweeps=sweeps,
            random_state=random_state,
        )
    if rule is None or _get_rule_source(rule) not in sources:
        raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
    read = _read_automaton(source, rule)
    if kind in {'injective', 'surjective', 'pre-injective'}:
        return _decide(read, kind, method=method, window=window, infinite=infinite)
    if kind in {'compose', 'difference'}:
        return _run_pair(read, kind, second=second, configuration=configuration, site=site, steps=steps)
    return _measure(
        read,
        kind,
        window=window,
        tries=tries,
        random_state=random_state,
        max_radius=max_radius,
        windows=windows,
        base=base,
    )

    def bind_analysis[ResultT](analysis: Callable[..., ResultT], **settings: object) -> partial[ResultT]:
    """Return an analysis with fixed settings, in the role of `make_scorer`.

    The bound analysis is a callable that takes the source alone. The bound analysis keeps the function in `func` and
    the settings in `keywords`, so experiments name their outputs after the function and pass it to other processes.

    Args:
        analysis:
            The analysis function, such as `entropy`.

        **settings:
            The settings of the analysis by name, as its keyword arguments take them.

    Returns:
        bound:
            The callable that applies the analysis with the settings to a source and returns its result.

    Raises:
        AnalysisError:
            The analysis is not callable, or it takes no setting of a given name.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import bind_analysis, rolling
        >>> variance = bind_analysis(rolling, kind='variance', window=3)
        >>> variance(np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0])).statistic.round(2).tolist()
        [[nan, nan, 0.22, 0.22]]
    """
    if not callable(analysis):
        error_msg = f'An analysis is a function of a source, not {analysis!r}.'
        raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
    try:
        inspect.signature(analysis).bind_partial(None, **settings)
    except TypeError as error:
        error_msg = f'{getattr(analysis, "__name__", analysis)!r} does not take these settings: {error}.'
        raise AnalysisError(error_msg) from error
    return partial(analysis, **settings)

    cell_complex(source, *, kind, space=None, variables=None)

    Return the Hodge decomposition, Betti numbers, or curved faces of a complex.

    The decomposition is of an edge state and the curved faces are those of angles. It reads a state of a group on a cell complex from a trajectory, or an array with the complex passed as space. An array of one dimension holds one snapshot, and an array of two dimensions one frame per row. Every result has one row per frame.

    The kind 'hodge' writes an edge state as the sum of the exterior derivative of a site potential, the transposed incidence of a face potential, and a remainder that both incidences map to 0. The three parts are orthogonal. The kind 'betti' reads the complex alone. The kind 'curvature' compares the oriented sum of an angle state around every face with the multiples of the period of the state, or of 2 pi for an array.

    It appears in many fields. It splits the flows of a network into gradient and cyclic parts, counts the holes of a pattern in topology, and finds the vortices of a lattice gauge field.

    def cell_complex(
    source: Source,
    *,
    kind: str,
    space: CellComplexSpace | None = None,
    variables: str | None = None,
) -> CellComplexResult:
    """Return the Hodge decomposition, Betti numbers, or curved faces of a complex.

    The decomposition is of an edge state and the curved faces are those of angles. It reads a state of a group on a
    cell complex from a trajectory, or an array with the complex passed as `space`. An array of one dimension holds one
    snapshot, and an array of two dimensions one frame per row. Every result has one row per frame.

    The kind `'hodge'` writes an edge state as the sum of the exterior derivative of a site potential, the transposed
    incidence of a face potential, and a remainder that both incidences map to 0. The three parts are orthogonal. The
    kind `'betti'` reads the complex alone. The kind `'curvature'` compares the oriented sum of an angle state around
    every face with the multiples of the period of the state, or of `2 pi` for an array.

    It appears in many fields. It splits the flows of a network into gradient and cyclic parts, counts the holes of a
    pattern in topology, and finds the vortices of a lattice gauge field.

    Args:
        source:
            The trajectory, an array of values on the edges, or `None` for the kind `'betti'` with a `space`.

        kind:
            `'hodge'`, `'betti'`, or `'curvature'`.

        space:
            The cell complex, or `None` for the complex of the group of `variables` on a trajectory.

        variables:
            The dotted name of the state of a trajectory, or `None` for a source that is an array.

    Returns:
        result:
            The complex, the values, and the results of the kind.

    Raises:
        AnalysisError:
            The kind is unknown, the source names no state of a cell complex, or the values do not fit the complex.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import cell_complex
        >>> from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import CellComplexSpace, LatticeSpace
        >>> space = CellComplexSpace(LatticeSpace((4, 4))).prepare()
        >>> cell_complex(None, kind='betti', space=space).betti
        (1, 2, 1)
        >>> uniform = np.r_[np.ones(16), np.zeros(16)]
        >>> hodge = cell_complex(uniform, kind='hodge', space=space)
        >>> bool(np.allclose(hodge.harmonic[0], uniform))
        True
    """
    _check_choice('cell_complex', 'kind', kind, KINDS)
    if space is not None and not isinstance(space, CellComplexSpace):
        error_msg = f'cell_complex reads a CellComplexSpace, not {space!r}.'
        raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
    values, period = (np.empty((0, 0)), DEFAULT_PERIOD) if source is None else _read_values(source, variables)
    found = _space_of(source, variables) if space is None and isinstance(source, Trajectory) else space
    if found is None:
        error_msg = 'cell_complex reads no complex. Give `space`, or the state of a group on a cell complex.'
        raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
    complex_space = found.prepare()
    if kind != 'betti' and values.shape[-1] != complex_space.incidences_[0].shape[0]:
        error_msg = (
            f'cell_complex reads {values.shape[-1]} values, but the complex has '
            f'{complex_space.incidences_[0].shape[0]} edges. Read a state of a group on its edges.'
        )
        raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
    if kind == 'hodge':
        return _hodge(complex_space, values, period)
    if kind == 'betti':
        return _betti(complex_space, values, period)
    return _curvature(complex_space, values, period)

    def chain_shape(
    source: Source,
    *,
    kind: str = 'gyration',
    group: str | None = None,
    reference: npt.ArrayLike | None = None,
) -> ChainShapeResult:
    """Return the geometry of a chain of points per frame.

    The chain is made of the positions of the members of a group in member order.

    It appears in many fields. It measures the size of a polymer, the end-to-end distance of a strand of DNA, and how
    far a folding protein lies from its native shape.

    Args:
        source:
            The trajectory, or an array of frames by points by dimensions.

        kind:
            `'gyration'` for the radius of gyration, `'end-to-end'` for the distance between the first and the last
            point, or `'rmsd'` for the root mean square deviation from `reference` after optimal superposition.

        group:
            The path of an agent or particle group of a trajectory, or the dotted name of a lattice state whose last
            axis holds the coordinates of a point, or `None` for the first agent or particle group.

        reference:
            The positions the deviation compares with, points by dimensions, for the kind `'rmsd'`.

    Returns:
        result:
            The positions and the value of every frame.

    Raises:
        AnalysisError:
            The kind is unknown, the kind `'rmsd'` has no reference, or the positions are not frames by points by
            dimensions.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import chain_shape
        >>> chain = np.array([[[0.0, 0.0], [3.0, 4.0]]])
        >>> chain_shape(chain, kind='end-to-end').values.tolist()
        [5.0]
    """
    _check_choice('chain_shape', 'kind', kind, SHAPE_KINDS)
    if kind == 'rmsd' and reference is None:
        error_msg = "chain_shape(kind='rmsd') compares with a reference. Pass `reference`."
        raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
    read = _read_positions(source, group) if isinstance(source, Trajectory) else source
    positions: Array = np.asarray(read, dtype=float)
    if positions.ndim != FRAME_DIMENSIONS:
        error_msg = f'chain_shape reads frames by points by dimensions, not the shape {positions.shape}.'
        raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
    centred = positions - positions.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    if kind == 'gyration':
        values = np.sqrt(np.mean(np.sum(centred**2, axis=2), axis=1))
    elif kind == 'end-to-end':
        values = np.linalg.norm(positions[:, -1] - positions[:, 0], axis=1)
    else:
        target = np.asarray(reference, dtype=float)
        target = target - target.mean(axis=0)
        values = np.array([_deviation(frame, target) for frame in centred])
    return ChainShapeResult(positions, values)

    clusters(source, *, kind='labels', variables=None, periodic=False, diagonal=False, axis=0, radius=None)

    Return the clusters of a grid, a graph, or points.

    They are the occupied cells of a grid, the components of a graph, or the contacts of points. The grid is a boolean array of any dimension, the last frame of a field of a trajectory, or a graph, the last network of a trajectory. Cells are connected through shared faces, or also corners with diagonal=True.

    With a radius, the source holds points instead, an array with one row per point, a stack of such arrays for the kind 'spanning', or the positions of a group of a trajectory in its last frame. Points closer than twice the radius are connected, and a cluster joins two opposite faces along axis when it holds points within the radius of both. The faces are those of the space of a trajectory, and those of the bounding box of an array.

    • 'labels': the label of every cell and the size of every cluster of a grid, in label order, and whether a cluster joins the two opposite edges of axis.
    • 'sizes': the size of every cluster of a grid or of every component of a graph, largest first.
    • 'percolation': the cluster sizes, the strength of the largest cluster, the mean cluster size, and spanning.
    • 'spanning': the share of the grids of an ensemble, stacked on the first axis or the frames of a trajectory, with a cluster joining the opposite edges of axis.

    It appears in many fields. It finds the percolating cluster of a porous rock, the burnt patches of a forest fire, and the groups of an opinion model.

    source Source

    periodic bool

    Whether clusters of a grid wrap around its edges.

    diagonal bool

    Whether cells that share only a corner are connected.

    def clusters(
    source: Source,
    *,
    kind: str = 'labels',
    variables: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    periodic: bool = False,
    diagonal: bool = False,
    axis: int = 0,
    radius: float | None = None,
) -> ClustersResult:
    """Return the clusters of a grid, a graph, or points.

    They are the occupied cells of a grid, the components of a graph, or the contacts of points. The grid is a boolean
    array of any dimension, the last frame of a field of a trajectory, or a graph, the last network of a trajectory.
    Cells are connected through shared faces, or also corners with `diagonal=True`.

    With a `radius`, the source holds points instead, an array with one row per point, a stack of such arrays for the
    kind `'spanning'`, or the positions of a group of a trajectory in its last frame. Points closer than twice the
    radius are connected, and a cluster joins two opposite faces along `axis` when it holds points within the radius of
    both. The faces are those of the space of a trajectory, and those of the bounding box of an array.

    - `'labels'`: the label of every cell and the size of every cluster of a grid, in label order, and whether a
      cluster joins the two opposite edges of `axis`.
    - `'sizes'`: the size of every cluster of a grid or of every component of a graph, largest first.
    - `'percolation'`: the cluster sizes, the strength of the largest cluster, the mean cluster size, and spanning.
    - `'spanning'`: the share of the grids of an ensemble, stacked on the first axis or the frames of a trajectory,
      with a cluster joining the opposite edges of `axis`.

    It appears in many fields. It finds the percolating cluster of a porous rock, the burnt patches of a forest fire,
    and the groups of an opinion model.

    Args:
        source:
            The grid or the grids, the graph, the points, or the trajectory.

        kind:
            The measure to compute, one of the kinds above.

        variables:
            The field of a trajectory to read, or `None` for its first field.

        periodic:
            Whether clusters of a grid wrap around its edges.

        diagonal:
            Whether cells that share only a corner are connected.

        axis:
            The axis whose two opposite edges a spanning cluster joins.

        radius:
            The contact radius of points, or `None` for grids and graphs.

    Returns:
        result:
            What the source was read as, and the measures of the kind.

    Raises:
        AnalysisError:
            The kind is unknown, a setting the kind does not read is changed, the radius is not positive or comes with
            settings of grids, or a kind that reads grids gets a graph.

    Examples:
        >>> import networkx as nx
        >>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import clusters
        >>> clusters([[1, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1]], kind='sizes').sizes.tolist()
        [2, 1]
        >>> clusters(nx.path_graph(3), kind='sizes').sizes.tolist()
        [3]
        >>> result = clusters([[1, 1, 0], [1, 0, 1]], kind='percolation')
        >>> result.strength, result.mean_size, result.spanning
        (0.5, 1.0, True)
        >>> clusters([[0, 0], [1, 0], [5, 5]], kind='sizes', radius=0.6).sizes.tolist()
        [2, 1]
    """
    _check_choice('clusters', 'kind', kind, KINDS)
    _check_settings(
        clusters,
        'kind',
        SETTINGS[kind] | {'variables'},
        kind=kind,
        variables=variables,
        periodic=periodic,
        diagonal=diagonal,
        axis=axis,
        radius=radius,
    )
    if radius is not None:
        if radius <= 0 or periodic or diagonal:
            error_msg = (
                f'clusters has radius={radius!r}, periodic={periodic!r}, and diagonal={diagonal!r}. A radius is '
                'positive, and points take neither of the settings of grids.'
            )
            raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
        points, faces = _read_points(source, kind, variables)
        return _of_points(points, faces, kind, axis, radius)
    if isinstance(source, nx.Graph):
        if kind in {'labels', 'spanning'}:
            error_msg = f'clusters of kind {kind!r} reads grids, not graphs. Use the kind sizes or percolation.'
            raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
        return _of_graph(source, kind)
    name = variables[0] if variables else None
    read = np.asarray(_read_fields(source, name), dtype=bool)
    if kind == 'spanning':
        spans = [_spans(_label(grid, periodic=False, diagonal=diagonal)[0], axis) for grid in read]
        return ClustersResult(grids=read, probability=float(np.mean(spans)))
    grids = read[-1:] if isinstance(source, Trajectory) else read[None]
    if kind == 'labels':
        labels, sizes = _label(grids[0], periodic=periodic, diagonal=diagonal)
        return ClustersResult(grids=grids, labels=labels, sizes=sizes, spanning=_spans(labels, axis))
    if kind == 'sizes':
        _, sizes = _label(grids[0], periodic=periodic, diagonal=diagonal)
        return ClustersResult(grids=grids, sizes=np.sort(sizes)[::-1])
    labels, sizes = _label(grids[0], periodic=False, diagonal=diagonal)
    ordered = np.sort(sizes)[::-1]
    strength, mean_size = _strength(ordered, grids[0].size)
    return ClustersResult(
        grids=grids,
        sizes=ordered,
        strength=strength,
        mean_size=mean_size,
        spanning=_spans(labels, axis),
    )

    coarse_grain(source, *, shape=(32, 32), box=None, values=None, over=None, state=None)

    Return agents coarse-grained into a field, or members into a density.

    The field lies on a grid, and the density is over the values of a state. An array holds one snapshot, one row per agent in the box. A trajectory gives the positions of its first agent or particle group at every frame, in the box of its space unless box is set, and one grid per frame.

    With over, the function coarse-grains in state space instead: every member counts at the given value nearest to its value of a state, and the field is the fraction of members at every value, which sums to 1. An array holds the values of one snapshot, one per member, or one row per frame, and a trajectory gives the values of the state state at every frame. The densities are the initial values of a distribution site group with one member per value.

    It appears in many fields. It turns animals into a density of a herd, traders into a distribution of wealth, and particles into a density field of a fluid.

    values ArrayLike | None

    		 None
    over ArrayLike | None

    The increasing values of a state to coarse-grain the members over, or None to coarse-grain positions.

    		 None
    state str | None

    The dotted name of the state whose values a trajectory gives, such as traders.wealth, with over.

    		 None

    Returns:

    def coarse_grain(
    source: Source,
    *,
    shape: Sequence[int] = (32, 32),
    box: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    values: npt.ArrayLike | None = None,
    over: npt.ArrayLike | None = None,
    state: str | None = None,
) -> CoarseGrainResult:
    """Return agents coarse-grained into a field, or members into a density.

    The field lies on a grid, and the density is over the values of a state. An array holds one snapshot, one row per
    agent in the box. A trajectory gives the positions of its first agent or particle group at every frame, in the box
    of its space unless `box` is set, and one grid per frame.

    With `over`, the function coarse-grains in state space instead: every member counts at the given value nearest to
    its value of a state, and the field is the fraction of members at every value, which sums to 1. An array holds the
    values of one snapshot, one per member, or one row per frame, and a trajectory gives the values of the state `state`
    at every frame. The densities are the initial values of a distribution site group with one member per value.

    It appears in many fields. It turns animals into a density of a herd, traders into a distribution of wealth, and
    particles into a density field of a fluid.

    Args:
        source:
            The trajectory, or an array of positions or of values of a state.

        shape:
            The number of cells along every side.

        box:
            The sides of the box, or `None` for the box of the space of a trajectory.

        values:
            One value or one row of values per agent of an array, such as unit directions for a polarization field, or
            `None` to count agents.

        over:
            The increasing values of a state to coarse-grain the members over, or `None` to coarse-grain positions.

        state:
            The dotted name of the state whose values a trajectory gives, such as `traders.wealth`, with `over`.

    Returns:
        result:
            The positions or values, the box, and the field.

    Raises:
        AnalysisError:
            A setting is invalid or missing, or the source holds no positions or values to coarse-grain.

    Examples:
        >>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import coarse_grain
        >>> positions = [[0.1, 0.1], [0.2, 0.1], [0.9, 0.9]]
        >>> coarse_grain(positions, shape=[2, 2], box=[1.0, 1.0]).field.tolist()
        [[2.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0]]
        >>> wealth = [-1.0, 0.4, 0.6, 1.5, 9.0]
        >>> coarse_grain(wealth, over=[0.0, 1.0, 2.0]).field.tolist()
        [0.4, 0.4, 0.2]
    """
    _check(shape, box, values, over, state)
    if over is not None:
        positions = _read_state(source, state)
        grid = np.asarray(over, dtype=float)
        frames = positions if positions.ndim == SNAPSHOT_DIMENSIONS else positions[None]
        densities = np.asarray([_get_density(row, grid) for row in frames])
        return CoarseGrainResult(positions, None, densities if positions.ndim == SNAPSHOT_DIMENSIONS else densities[0])
    if isinstance(source, Trajectory):
        snapshots = _read_snapshots(source)
        if snapshots.positions is None:
            error_msg = 'The agents of the trajectory have no positions with coordinates to coarse-grain.'
            raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
        positions = snapshots.positions
        sides = box if box is not None else snapshots.box
    else:
        positions = np.asarray(source, dtype=float)
        sides = box
    if sides is None:
        error_msg = 'coarse_grain needs the sides of the box. Set `box`.'
        raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
    read_box = np.asarray(sides, dtype=np.float64)
    if len(shape) != read_box.size:
        error_msg = f'The shape {tuple(shape)} needs one entry per dimension of the box, {read_box.size}.'
        raise AnalysisError(error_msg)
    if positions.ndim > SNAPSHOT_DIMENSIONS:
        field = np.asarray([_get_field(frame, shape, read_box, values) for frame in positions])
    else:
        field = _get_field(positions, shape, read_box, values)
    return CoarseGrainResult(positions, read_box, field)

    complexity(source, *, variables=None, dimension=6, delay=1, ties='order', random_state=None)

    Return the place of series or field frames on Rosso's complexity-entropy plane.

    It covers every series of a source, or every frame of a field. The entropy is the normalized permutation entropy of the ordinal patterns, and the complexity is that entropy times the Jensen-Shannon divergence of the patterns from uniform ones, computed with ordpy. Noise has entropy near 1 and complexity near 0, regular series both near 0, and chaos lies in between with high complexity.

    It appears in many fields. It tells chaos from noise in heart beats, in climate records, and in the prices of a market.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
